name: Geneva initiative IN 185 committee (Jean Batou) and backing parties
why: Cantonal initiative for a 2.5 per mille solidarity contribution on fortunes over CHF 3m for ten years; voted 18 June 2023. The official texts read do not name the committee or parties.
note: Debate of 1 Sept 2022 read: Batou (EAG), Eckert (Greens), Thevoz (SP) added; committee list and parties still not found.

name: Neuchâtel POP initiative "Pour une fiscalité plus équitable"
why: Higher wealth-tax rate from CHF 500,000, filed by the POP in 2017, rejected 15 May 2022.
note: Voter pamphlet unreadable (ne.ch returns a web page); POP Neuchatel added from Le Matin. PS, Solidarites and Greens as backers still unverified.

name: St. Gallen initiative for a progressive wealth-tax scale
why: Would replace the flat rate by a three-step scale; sponsors not yet identified.
note: The St. Gallen initiative was voted on 14 June 2015 (73% no); SP and Greens St. Gallen added from NZZ. ratsinfo.sg.ch blocks scripts.

name: Aargau initiative "Millionärssteuer" (2016, rejected with 74.6% no)
why: Cantonal ballot on a tax on millionaires; check design (wealth versus income) and sponsors.
note: Official 2018 booklet gives no sponsor names; see D0014.

name: Patrick Hässig (Green Liberals): federal wealth tax with CHF 5m exemption
why: Reported proposal after the Juso vote; Blick blocks plain fetches (403), so read it in a browser or find the motion in Curia Vista.
note: Hassig and the GLP added from nau.ch and 20 Minuten; Blick page still blocked.

name: Schweizerischer Gewerkschaftsbund (SGB/USS)
why: National union federation; a position on a wealth tax in its own publications would give the largest union actor. No source found yet.
note: Searched twice for an SGB/USS statement on a wealth tax: found only a 2021 referendum on stamp duty. Read sgb.ch in a browser.

name: Oxfam Switzerland, Alliance Sud, Public Eye
why: Tax-justice NGOs; check each for a statement naming a wealth tax.
note: Alliance Sud and Dominik Gross added (Infosperber copy of the commentary; alliancesud.ch is behind a bot check, not bypassed). Oxfam Switzerland, Public Eye, Attac Schweiz, Greenpeace Schweiz, Swiss churches/Caritas: searched, no wealth-tax statement found (Caritas 2012 paper rejected a one-off levy).

name: Isabel Martínez (ETH Zurich, KOF)
why: Co-author of a paper on a progressive wealth tax in Switzerland; the paper describes effects, so she needs an op-ed or interview calling for the tax before she can be added.
note: The E4S white paper 'Wealth and Inheritance in 21st-Century Switzerland' (Brulhart, Fuster, Martinez, Moseka, Feb 2026) was read: it is descriptive and makes no recommendation of a wealth tax, so co-authors other than Brulhart (who advocates it in the SRF piece) are not added.

name: "Wealth and Inheritance" study (Brülhart and colleagues, Feb 2026)
why: The study named in the SRF piece; its co-authors at ETH Zurich and EPFL may recommend a wealth tax.

name: SP strategy paper 2020 proposing a special wealth tax above CHF 500 million
why: Would give the SP actor a manifesto-type row from its own document; the SP document itself is not yet found.

name: Earlier National Council and Council of States votes on wealth-tax motions 2010 to 2019
why: Query Business by title for SP, Green and PdA motions; take the Ja votes as in H0001 to H0003. No title with Vermögenssteuer, Solidaritätsabgabe or Millionäre showed a wealth-tax request before 2020 apart from the 2013 Pauschalbesteuerung initiative (lump-sum taxation, outside the definition).

name: Grand Conseil of Geneva: tax commission report and plenary vote on IN 185 and the counter-proposal (early 2023)
why: Commission report and vote lists would name more deputies backing the contribution.

name: Tamedia/20 Minuten (Leewas) post-vote poll, March 2026: support for a federal wealth tax above CHF 5 million
why: A poll on exactly a wealth tax for meta.json; headlines say 68% in favour, but the figure is not in the readable page text.
note: Browser: Tages-Anzeiger summary confirms 68% for a federal wealth tax on large fortunes; added to meta.json polls. Question wording and sample size are behind the paywall.

name: Volksinitiative committee "Millionärssteuer - Für eine faire Vermögenssteuer im Aargau" (voted 23 Sept 2018)
why: The official voter booklet gives the committee text but names no party; find the sponsors (SP Aargau, Greens, unions?).

name: Signatory lists of the Davos letters (Patriotic Millionaires, Millionaires for Humanity, "We Must Draw the Line" 2025/2026)
why: Signatories living in Switzerland would be wealthy supporters with a signed statement; press reports give no Swiss names apart from Jan Colruyt.
note: timetowin.world/signatories read in the browser: 366 signatories, six marked CH; five added (Colruyt was already in). The Patriotic Millionaires 2025 letter list was not checked.

why: Web search found no initiative to raise the wealth tax in these four cantons; the cantonal parliament databases might still hold motions by left deputies.
note: Browser pass: Basel-Stadt Grosser Rat (Geschaeftsverzeichnis Nov 2026 and a 2022 written question by Beda Baumgartner on wealth concentration: an information request, not support) has no wealth-tax motion; Ticino: Greens' initiative of 10 Dec 2025 added; Bern: Greens press release added as grade C (opposes a wealth-tax cut), no Grosser Rat motion to raise it found; Vaud done. Not read: Bern Grosser Rat Geschaeftsdatenbank directly, Ticino Gran Consiglio database (PS 2021 plan for higher wealth rates seen in La Regione only).

why: The vote on the one-year surcharge and the committee referral of the 0.2-0.5% tax above CHF 10m would name every deputy who supported them; the 3 November 2026 sitting is after this run.

why: The 2024 and 2026 letters have lists with country codes (one and six Swiss names); the 2025 letter list was not found.
note: Find the campaign site of the 2025 letter (the Fortune piece is by a signatory).

why: Said the Juso will keep fighting for fair taxation of large wealth after the 30 Nov 2025 defeat; a statement naming a wealth tax would qualify.
